project_type: Python Telegram Bot (Telethon-based) - dual-bot architecture for Rubika subscription service
test_framework: No formal test framework detected. Validation via Docker build and syntax checking.
test_command: python -c "import customer_bot; import owner_bot; import tron; import db; import config; print('OK')"
verification_instructions: 1. Run python syntax check on all modified files. 2. Docker build to verify dependencies. 3. Import all modules to verify no import errors.
environment_constraints: Open internet available. No .env file present (only .env.example). Module-level imports may fail without valid .env values but syntax/import checks are still possible.
contribution_requirements: No CONTRIBUTING.md. Follow existing code conventions: Persian UI text, logbus for all logging, db.py for all data access, config.py for settings.
key_patterns: 1. customer_bot.py uses state dict for conversation flow, _gate() for access control, _respond() for CB/message response. 2. tron.py returns VerifyResult(ok, reason, amount, to_address, confirmed). 3. db.py uses sqlite3 with _conn() factory, init() for schema creation. 4. config.py loads from .env with _int/_float/_bool helpers. 5. logbus.event(title, rows, pv_user) for centralized logging. 6. owner_bot.py uses is_owner() guard, safe_edit() for response, state dict for conversation.
directory_structure: Flat structure at root. /data/ holds SQLite DBs and Telethon sessions. Two bots run from same codebase via MODE env var. tron.py handles on-chain verification. db.py is the customer operational DB. central_db.py is owner-only.
